title: Hidden gauge invariance
summary: The role of gauge invariance is reconsidered by "deriving it without assuming it" within an autonomous approach to interactions of Standard Model particles. In this approach, the renormalizable interactions are purely constrained by quantum principles, notably the representation on a Hilbert space, which forces interactions to be "string-localized". To some surprise, most interactions fulfilling the constraints enjoy an emergent but possibly "hidden" gauge invariance (uncovered via redefinitions of quantum fields).
